I farm only 1.2 mu, and I am 72, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation simple, steady, and within what I can manage myself. I will plant winter wheat on all 1.2 mu first, then summer maize on the same 1.2 mu after wheat harvest. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water rather than gambling on rain, but I will still keep irrigation to the key growth stages so I do not add unnecessary labor or cost. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in at planting with a moderate nitrogen rate, and use rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing on such a small plot. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger stand and better yield on the same land after wheat. I will keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and spray only enough to control the common diseases, insects, and weeds. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a reliable harvest from both crops with work intensity I can still handle.
